page: Amazon Web Services m8a.48xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 192 dedicated physical cores across 192 vCPUs running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz without multithreading overhead. Memory infrastructure consists of 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and hardware cryptography acceleration.

Network connectivity features a 75 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs, requiring external network-attached storage architectures such as Amazon EBS for persistent data storage. Compute and memory benchmarks consistently place the instance in top percentiles, marked by a multi-core stress-ng metric of 703523.15, a Geekbench multi-core score of 28600.0, and a Clang software compilation score of 90714.0. Large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 1032.49 GB/sec alongside uncached write bandwidth of 451.46 GB/sec.

Hardware-level efficiency derives from high parallel compute density coupled with DDR5 memory throughput, which drives throughput metrics such as 466.87 million Redis SET operations per second and 165.56 GB/sec in static web serving. While text generation on large language models shows typical CPU-bound limitations, prompt processing throughput remains high across small, medium, and 70B parameter models. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage represents an operational tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage planning. The instance fits large enterprise deployments, distributed compilation pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory databases, compute-intensive data processing, and large microservice clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.48xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud server equipped with 192 dedicated physical cores running on AMD EPYC 9R45 processors at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM at 6 GHz, adhering to a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio, along with a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local storage and no GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth exceeding 1000 GB/sec for large reads, and high in-memory key-value execution reaching over 466 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware cost efficiency is driven by high single-socket core density and fast memory subsystems. The m8a.48xlarge is well fitted for high-throughput in-memory caching, distributed build farms, static web serving infrastructure, and massive parallel general-purpose enterprise applications.
